Birdseye is one of tailoring's great little cheats: clean and classic from afar, properly interesting up close. This grey wool-blend blazer is cut in a sharp tailored fit, so it does the smart work for you without tipping into full boardroom cosplay.
Style it with matching tailoring and a striped silk tie from our Men's Suits collection, or keep things a touch more relaxed by pairing it with some denim jeans.
Q: What is birdseye wool, and is it good for suits?
A: Birdseye wool is a micro-patterned suiting fabric created by weaving tiny, contrasting dots into a darker backdrop, resulting in a pattern that looks like a small bird’s eye up close. From a few feet away, it registers as a clean, solid tone, but up close, it reveals an incredible depth of texture.
Is it good for suits? It is quite literally one of the best suiting fabrics ever made. Birdseye is a favourite among tailors because the intricate micro-weave hides day-to-day wear, naturally resists wrinkles, and strikes the perfect balance between formal elegance and tactile interest.

Designed by Andersen-Andersen in Denmark, the “Marine” crew neck uses a 12-gauge pure wool knit to create a light-to-medium-weight sweater, ideal for cool summer evenings and autumnal layering. Knitted and linked in Italy, this fully fashioned knit features a symmetrical design — meaning the front and back are identical, allowing the sweater to be worn either way around. In the past, this symmetry made it easier for sailors to dress in the dark. However, Andersen-Andersen honours the tradition for a more sustainable reason, believing that rotating a sweater reduces wear in any one spot, thereby extending its life.
As for the wool itself, Andersen-Andersen’s signature yarn is made from mulesing-free, 100% pure new wool sourced from Corriedale sheep in Patagonia. The fibres are carefully cleansed and worsted to remove broken and short fibres before being given an extra spin to create a denser, more durable yarn that is far less likely to pill. So while this particular sweater is considered a medium-light style, it offers the same level of strength and longevity as the brand’s heavier-gauge knits.
